body:
You are drafting DIALOGUE LINES for a video game. Reply in plain text only, in the exact format asked. No commentary.

## The game
"The Crooked Moon" is a single-player turn-based tactical party RPG (fully voiced, branching dialogue, skill checks, a storyteller Narrator). Folk-horror campaign set in Druskenvald, an afterlife realm of endless night under a gargantuan crescent moon with a leering crone's face. Drawn like a 1960s monster cartoon stuck in Halloween, but the story is real folk horror: stakes, doomed innocents, sacrifice. Humour is deadpan and sits inside the dread. Everything is our own invention in our own words.

## This chapter: Maidenmist Cemetery
South-east of the village of Wickermoor, an endless fogbound cemetery fenced with cold iron is really a prison built over a tear into the Shroud, the mist of death that rings the realm. Wrathful soul-stripped spirits called the shrouded would pour out of it. Its sexton is YORGRIM, the ghost of an orc seer of the Shadestone Clan, who was tricked by his chieftain into a ritual that annihilated his whole clan's souls; he drags a gravestone carved with their names chained to his back as penance. He is dour, stoic, few words, never cruel, tells what matters, and grows vaguer and more distracted as the chapter goes; deep slow orc bass, short flat sentences, long pauses. His spectral black hound ISOLDE (white eyes, a hooded lantern in her mouth) does not speak: only the Narrator describes her. He asked five friends to kindle balefire beacons from fragments of their souls: Sir Marius Renathyr (knight of a morning god, horse Dawn, King Viktor Denathria), Lethica Nightborne (priestess of the Nightmother, barn owl, loved Marius), Ol' Jericho Sticks (kindly scarecrow banjo man), Captain Briggsy Kratch (pirate with a heart of gold, lucky, a swordsman and schemer), Farryn of the Greenwood (satyr druid of the Green Queen, loved Gwenna). They fell to the Horned King's sin and the heroes (the player's party of four, level nine) killed them. The beacons went dark, the tear grew, the dead walked into Wickermoor. The heroes relight the beacons with Final Rites that honour who the Fallen were before they fell, then go below, where Yorgrim breaks and becomes the Chained Reaper; they destroy him and perform his own rites to seal the tear.
Wickermoor people: MORI SHADE, undertaker, grave, stately, white hair, all black, a fount of folklore, follows the Strangers' ways learned from Yorgrim; DORIS SQUIRE, constable, tall, stocky, says the fewest words possible, flat northern burr; TOBIAS DIBBS, Mori's apprentice, relentlessly cheerful and practical; HESTER BOLTON, annoyed her husband Gregor is now a ghast and still owes rent; ADELA DRUSKENVALD (transatlantic 1920s patter); WESTON MURDOCH (warm revival preacher); Theodora Mayville the postmaster is secretly a pigeon hag.

## The Narrator
The Narrator is the Vagrant, a frog-faced ferryman telling the tale afterwards: warm, folksy, wry, fond of the party; never gloats. Second person, present tense, only what a hero could perceive, concrete senses (smell, sound, texture), no game words (HP, roll, level, check, DC, save), no modern slang, never "suddenly". Never name a specific hero (the party is addressed as "you" or "the party").

## Format rules
- One line of plain text per key, written as `key: text`. No quotes around the text, no stage directions, no asterisks, no emoji, no em dashes (use commas, periods, colons), straight quotes only, no brackets.
- A spoken line is one to three short sentences, 12 to 38 words, never over 45. Narrator lines are one or two sentences, never over 45 words. People speak plainly in their own voice; they do not explain the plot to the audience.
- Obey each brief's sentence count and content. Every line must carry a concrete detail.
- Do not put speaker names at the start of the text. Do not repeat the brief.


## Lines to draft (key | speaker | mood | brief). Reply with one `key: text` line for each key and nothing else.

result:
necrolisk_herbs: You hurl the reeking herbal brew into the beast's maw, and with a wet, sour wrench it heaves half its last meal onto the stones.
mori_hub: Tell me then, with the ink still wet upon my ledger, how fares the cold iron watch out in Maidenmist Cemetery tonight?
walk_crimson: Setting her lantern down, Isolde noses through the cold grey ash of the crimson brazier and nudges out a small wooden horse carved by Yorgrim's patient hand.
walk_violet: At the mossy foot of the violet fountain, Isolde sniffs the damp flagstones and paws loose a pale mask of polished bone that Yorgrim tucked away.
walk_emerald: Isolde burrows her black snout beneath the knotted emerald roots and draws out a fragrant sprig of dried greenery bound with coarse thread.
enter_mm_gate: Fifteen-foot spears of cold iron vanish into the wet grey wool of the fog on either hand. Between two stone reapers, the bent gate hangs open with a rust-bitten groan.
enter_mm_corpse_road: Smooth cobbles slick with grease and rain run wide enough for a hearse between the leaning stones. The fog presses against your throats like wet linen, smelling of turned clay.
enter_mm_sepulcher: Seven paved paths climb through drifting blue-green wisps to a cracked, moss-furred tomb. Six empty iron sconces flank its colossal doors, cold and waiting in the mist.
enter_mm_highborn_crypts: Dark polished marble gleams under the leering snouts of rain-streaked gargoyles while bats wheel overhead. A single iron brazier holds a bed of dull red coals that barely warms the damp.
enter_mm_crypt_below: Frost bites at your knuckles as you step down among rows of heavy stone sarcophagi. High in the vaults, roosting bats shift and chitter above the smell of old dust.
enter_mm_cremation_gardens: Cold rain drums hard upon the red brick walks, washing past rows of clay urns and overflowing basins. Somewhere in the drench, an iron bell tolls a slow, sodden measure.
enter_mm_potters_field: Plain wooden stakes lean over sunken, nameless sod while wet crows mutter in the mire. Pale amber lanterns drift low through the fog without a hand to carry them.
enter_mm_mausoleum_lanes: Ivy-choked vaults rise out of the bog like a sunken town, their cracked stones weeping black water. Every step sucks at your boots and sends up a sharp, sour stench of rot.
enter_mm_burial_mounds: Great grassy barrows swell from the mire, crowned by twisted trees with solemn faces grown into their bark. Boughs shaped like crooked fingers offer up apples way too red and sweet for a graveyard.
enter_mm_shadestone_sanctuary: Tall standing stones scored deep with orcish names ring a low ziggurat where an azure flame burns clear. Here the wind falls hush, holding a clean, cold stillness the rest of the graveyard has forgotten.
enter_mm_kings_rest: Before a palatial barrow rises the colossus of an armored king, his stone blade thrust into the boiling mist. Steel rings and dead men shout at its doors, fighting a war that never heard it ended.
enter_mm_balefire_chamber: Six iron sconces line this sixty-foot hall of fitted stone, waiting for their differently colored flames. At the far end, a tumbled choke of rubble leaks a slow, freezing draft of grey mist.
enter_mm_undercroft: Thousands of yellowing skulls stare from the packed dirt walls while pale mist pools around your ankles. A low shudder runs through the earthen floor, rattling dry teeth in their sockets.
enter_mm_necropolis_depths: Great gouges of torn rock mark where something huge clawed this cavern wide, leaving trails of pale green slime. Half-eaten dead folk jut from burrows in the muck, lit by a sickly, dripping glow.
enter_mm_tomb: Three-pronged iron platforms hang on massive chains over a pit lit by cold blue-green balefire. Above them, the very air splits open like frayed cloth, bleeding freezing mist and a sound like weeping wind.
enter_mm_gravestones_a: Rolling hills of crowded headstones tilt into the fog, packed so close your cloaks brush the wet lichen. Out between the rows, boots shuffle through the dead grass, always a few paces out of sight.
enter_mm_gravestones_b: Crooked markers crowd shoulder to shoulder across the sodden hills as far as the mist allows. Something heavy keeps pace with you behind the stones, stopping whenever you stop to listen.
